literal: Good manliness is, for a person, making the dignity of the family they were born in, and taking it upon themselves.
translation: True manliness for a person consists in taking upon themselves the responsibility to elevate and lead the family in which they were born.
modern: ஒருவனுக்குச் சிறந்த ஆண்மை என்பது, தான் பிறந்த குடும்பத்தை ஆளும் பொறுப்பை ஏற்று அதை மேம்படுத்துவதாகும்.
explanation: The couplet defines true manliness or noble effort (நல்லாண்மை) not as mere physical strength or individual success, but as the dedication to uplift one's own family. The word 'ஆண்மை' (manliness/strength) is used twice: first as 'நல்லாண்மை' (true/noble effort) and then as 'இல்லாண்மை' (family leadership/management). The poet explains that a person's ultimate strength is demonstrated when they take charge of their family's welfare and elevate its status. This active responsibility (ஆக்கிக் கொளல்) is what constitutes genuine dignity and duty.
